To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a power control strategy has proposed for a low voltage multibus microgrid.
a novel power control strategy is developed for a low-voltagemultibus microgrid.

an accurate power control strategy is developed for a low-volt microgrid, where a virtual inductor is employed to prevent the coupling between real and reactive powers, an accurate reactive power sharing strategy is proposed by compensating the effects of impedance voltage drops, and the effects of DGs’ local loads are considered to further improve the reactive power sharing accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the power control and sharing of power-electronics-interfaced DG units in a low-volume multibus microgrid and proposes a power control strategy to improve the reactive power control precision and accuracy.
the power control strategy for power-electronics-interfaced distributed generation units operating in a low-voltaged multibus microgrid.
the development of a novel power control strategy for power-electronics-interfaced DG units operating in a low-voltagemultibus microgrid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed power control strategy can achieve accurate active and reactive power control and accurate power sharing in low-voltage microgrids, even with the unequal impedance among DG units, unequal DG local load locations, and the mainly resistive network line impedances.
the proposed power control strategy can achieve accurate power sharing and control in a low-volatge multibus microgrid with resistive line and DG local load effects.
the proposed control strategy is accurate and effective for a low-volatge multibus microgrid with power-electronics-interfaced DG units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed control strategy is able to accurately share the real and reactive power among DG units and the loads in a low-voltagedistributed generation microgrid.

this paper proposes a new power control strategy to accurately control and share the active and reactive powers for DG units operating in a multibus low-voltage microgrids, where the conventional power droop control method is unpractical.
the proposed power control strategy is accurate and practical for a low-volatage multibus microgrid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed power control strategy can achieve accurate real and reactive power sharing and control in low-voltage multibus microgrids.
the accurate reactive power sharing and control is critical to the operation of the microgrids.
the power control accuracy can be improved by using a virtual inductance at the interfacing converter output and an accurate control algorithm.
